original_test_intent: Inject an uncorrectable TXWAFL fault at the intended IOD endpoint, verify the approved containment/reset and fresh IOD-specific RAS report, then prove the TX path, attached I/O and host have recovered.
original_method: Enumerate TXWAFL links and bind link0/errorlocation0 to a physical socket/IOD/TX endpoint; preserve raw state and logs; validate errortype1 and severity; run one injection under OOB capture; correlate fresh IOD MCA/CPER/AER/BERT and reset evidence; test link and representative attached-I/O traffic; restore BIOS/HDT/threshold state.
manual_activity: The FAE resolves the severity conflict, proves link0/errorlocation0 targets the intended IOD, approves containment, performs one injection under independent console and restores the TXWAFL/IOD path.
required_inputs: Vendor proof errortype1 is IOD UCE and decision on contradictory correctable Criteria
FF5/FFE threshold encoding, TXWAFL relevance and raw restoration values
Expected containment/reset and fresh IOD-specific MCA/CPER/AER/BERT/SEL fields
Supported OS, timeout, attached-I/O traffic and link recovery thresholds
Abort, OOB recovery, injector cleanup and full BIOS/HDT restoration
safety_requirements: Dedicated SUT with independent OOB console and quiesced non-production I/O
Preserve raw baselines and do not infer link0 from ordinal position
Inject once only after severity, endpoint and recovery plan approval
Abort on wrong source/severity, unexpected reset, boot failure, persistent link/AER error, device loss or missing fresh record
No automatic retry/reset; restore all changed settings and verify attached devices
agent_execution_scope: Validate topology, tuple, severity, threshold, evidence and recovery contracts
Collect read-only enumeration, settings, OOB timeline, MCA/CPER/AER/BERT/SEL and link/device health
Do not select target, modify BIOS/HDT, inject, reset, recover, retry or decide verdict
engineer_actions: Approve IOD topology and tuple semantics
Resolve severity/PASS rule and containment oracle
Restore state, validate I/O health and issue verdict

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Generic WAFL/TXWAFL/uncorrected text and an SEL tail do not prove link0 maps to the IOD or that a fresh errortype1 UCE caused the observed outcome.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: After vendor mapping and severity approval, inject the single IOD tuple under OOB capture and require fresh endpoint-specific durable records plus recovered TXWAFL and attached-I/O health.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: linknumber0, errorlocation0, errortype1, FF5-to-FFE threshold, three OS families and 15/20-minute values remain preserved but gated.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a topology-bound IOD UCE injection with fresh durable endpoint attribution and measured link/device recovery.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds severity reconciliation, physical mapping, raw rollback, endpoint fields, containment deadlines and I/O health checks.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Tool PASS plus a generic dmesg line cannot establish IOD coverage or post-UCE data-path health.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A wrong or persistent IOD fault may reset the SUT, isolate multiple devices or damage in-flight I/O.

project_override_considerations: If runtime enumeration does not map numeric link 0 to the intended IOD, do not substitute another link without a reviewed topology update; preserve the original tuple as a recorded source discrepancy.
expected_evidence: Physical socket/IOD/TXWAFL and attached-device topology plus raw enumeration
Approved tool/spec and tuple/severity mapping with raw settings baseline
Exact injection transcript and OOB containment/reset/boot timeline
Fresh IOD-specific MCA/CPER/AER/BERT/SEL source and severity
Recovered link counters, attached-device enumeration and bounded I/O integrity

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The title, procedure and errortype describe an uncorrectable IOD fault while Criteria says correctable. Numeric link0/errorlocation0 has no authoritative IOD mapping, and threshold relevance, exact containment, fresh endpoint signature, OS timeout and recovery limits are absent.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The intended TXWAFL IOD UCE and exact source tuple are identifiable. Static review completes with execution gated on engineering resolution.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Reliability row 79 Wistron-System RAS-00799-V002: decide the correctable Criteria versus TXWAFL IOD Uncorrectable title/errortype1; prove linknumber0/errorlocation0 maps to the required socket/IOD/TX endpoint; define FF5/FFE relevance, expected containment/reset and fresh IOD-specific MCA/CPER/AER/BERT/SEL fields; approve OS, timeout, attached-I/O recovery thresholds, aborts, OOB recovery and restoration.

review_improvement: Adds IOD endpoint attribution and attached-I/O recovery while explicitly preventing the contradictory correctable line or a generic log from becoming the acceptance oracle.
independent_technical_reasoning: TXWAFL at an IOD may affect several downstream devices, so OS return alone does not show that the transmit fabric or I/O topology recovered. Numeric link0 can vary with platform topology, and errorlocation0 only implies IOD because the source says so. The severity conflict must be resolved before defining whether reset is required, and fresh CPER/AER source identifiers must correlate the event to the intended IOD.
